stock_segments.discussion_summary: Detailed discussion of Vertisit, Peter's largest position at 30%. Company provides large LED screens and digital signage solutions for automotive retail (Volkswagen, Lamborghini, BMW) and retail (Uniqlo). Currently undergoing major inflection from hardware/software mix to primarily SaaS platform. Valuation appears optically high due to recent acquisitions not fully reflected, but trades at attractive ~3x ARR and ~5x EBITDA. Strong execution track record with 40 quarters of sequential ARR growth and profitable since 2009. Pending acquisition of MultiQ to add 50m ARR and customer base at reasonable valuation with significant cost synergies. Management including CEO Johan Lind owns ~50% of company. Company is approaching fund threshold size (~500m SEK) attracting institutional interest.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg
quotes.text: Det är ett case som... det är svårt att hitta fel tycker jag. Dels har de en väldigt spännande inflektionspunkt just nu. Där de väljer att göra ett skifte och outsourza mycket av det som har sämre marginaler. Det vill säga hårdvarudelen. Och så vill de liksom vara en plattformsleverantör.

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Comprehensive discussion of Sea Limited, Peter's holding for 2 years. Southeast Asian technology leader with three business pillars: e-commerce (Shopee marketplace), gaming (Free Fire), and fintech (SeaMoney). Market leader across Southeast Asian markets with superior execution against Alibaba's Lazada. Shopee grew larger than Shopify in 6 years with faster revenue growth. Company facing short-term headwinds: India banned Free Fire gaming app, major shareholder Tencent sold shares to address regulatory concerns, and company withdrew from India due to unpredictable regulators. Despite these challenges, long-term thesis intact due to enormous growth opportunity. Southeast Asia has 75% unbanked/underbanked population and low e-commerce penetration (5-10% vs 30% in China/UK). E-commerce historically provides optionality to expand into adjacent verticals like payments and logistics.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg
quotes.text: Sea Limited köpte jag för två år sedan. Det är ett bolag som har tre olika affärsben. De är stora inom e-handel, gaming och även fintech. Det är ett ben som växer fram just nu.

quotes.text: Precis som namnet antyder opererar de i Sudostasien. Det är därför de heter SEA, South East Asia. De är marknadsledare på alla betydande marknader som de är på. De har exekverat väldigt väl. De har slagit Alibabas dotterbolag, Lazada på fingrarna i Sudostasien.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg
quotes.text: På Shopee på bara sex år har det växt till att bli större än Shopify till exempel. När det kommer till omsättning och växer mycket snabbare. Så de har gjort någonting väldigt bra här.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg

stock_segments.discussion_summary: Detailed discussion of Smart Eye, a Swedish AI software company for automotive Driver Monitoring Systems (DMS). Company is one of the strongest players in its specific niche of advanced AI software for vehicle safety. Regulatory requirements kicking in between 2022-2025 in USA, Europe, and China will force entire automotive industry to adopt DMS technology. Smart Eye has won approximately 70% of market share in Design Wins (uphanded contracts). Operates in a duopoly with Seeing Machines, meaning they and the competitor control essentially the entire market. Strong visibility into revenue due to regulatory mandate rather than discretionary spending. Stock has declined nearly 50% in a year, but Peter remains unconcerned, focusing on 2025-2026 thesis when regulations fully implemented. Differentiation from Seeing Machines: Smart Eye's software is hardware-agnostic and can work with any camera system, while Seeing Machines has specific hardware partnerships. Peter not focused on short-term price movements.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg
quotes.text: Det är lagkrav som kickar in mellan 2022 och 2025 som kommer att tvinga hela bilindustrin. Det är USA, Europa, Kina att adoptera den här tekniken.

quotes.speaker: Peter Westberg

summary: Peter Westberg (Matematikern) discusses his concentrated investment philosophy with 5 holdings: Vertisit (30%), Sea Limited, Mercado Libre, Smart Eye, and Evolution. Portfolio down 25% in Q1 2022 after being up 40% annually for 4 years, due to war in Ukraine and tech correction. Prefers concentrated portfolio of 5-10 stocks to spend more time on each case. Values founder-led companies with significant insider ownership. All current holdings are long-term positions despite recent volatility. Sold Pinterest due to poor IR and communication. Co-founded Kalkyl analysis firm acquired by Spotlight.
key_takeaways: Concentrated portfolio approach with 5-10 holdings allows deeper research
Values founder-led companies with significant insider ownership like Vertisit (50%)
Accepts volatility in high-beta growth stocks like Mercado Libre and Sea Limited
Regulatory-driven growth in Smart Eye provides strong visibility
Uses Twitter for networking and investment idea discovery
Sold Pinterest due to poor IR and lack of clarity on strategic direction
